clue.text: Plant obtained from mean, dark criminal

indicators.note: something criminal is bent or crooked, so the preceding words are twisted out of their order

blocks.note: taken as written, eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A sinister herb is extracted from some nasty, shadowy wrongdoer.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma between mean and dark is just surface punctuation; both words go into the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: The mandrake is a Mediterranean herb of the nightshade family with a forked root, long linked with magic and folklore.

clue.text: Fellow, married since September 29

blocks.note: Michael stands for any fellow, a man's name
M is the abbreviation for married
as in the sense of because

explanation.surface: A man has been married ever since a particular autumn date.
explanation.walkthrough: Since looks like it governs the date, but it only means as, because. Michaelmas is an English quarter day and the name of Oxford and Cambridge's autumn term.
explanation.definitionFit: Michaelmas is the Feast of St Michael and All Angels, celebrated on the twenty-ninth of the ninth month.

clue.text: Make tough operator find weapon of mass destruction

blocks.note: to nerve is to steel or toughen oneself
an agent is an operative, one who operates for another

explanation.surface: A hardened spy uncovers a doomsday device.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerve agents such as sarin are chemical weapons capable of killing large numbers, classed among weapons of mass destruction.

clue.text: Girl consuming a yogurt dish

indicators.note: consuming means eating, taking something inside, so the name wraps around the next piece

blocks.note: Rita is a girl's name
taken as written

explanation.surface: A young woman tucks into a yogurt-based side dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Raita is an Indian side dish of yogurt mixed with cucumber or other vegetables and spices.

clue.text: Nervous ladies cope OK in complicated circumstances

indicators.note: nervous suggests jittery and agitated, so the letters that follow are shaken into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, twelve letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Anxious women manage fine when things get tricky.
explanation.definitionFit: A kaleidoscope figuratively means a constantly shifting, intricate pattern of events, hence a complex changing situation.

clue.text: Medicine man has treated bloke

indicators.note: treated suggests something processed or worked on, so the letters of the word before it are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
a bloke is a man in informal British speech

explanation.surface: A tribal healer has given some fellow medical treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Treated' reads as medical care to suit the medicine man, but it only shuffles the three letters before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaman is a tribal healer and spirit intermediary, the figure loosely called a medicine man among many peoples.

clue.text: It's sweet to wander aimlessly for a short, happy period

blocks.note: honey is a sweet substance made by bees
to moon about is to wander around idly and dreamily

explanation.surface: A romantic claims drifting about without purpose is a delightful way to spend a brief interlude.
explanation.definitionFit: Besides the holiday after a wedding, a honeymoon is any brief early spell of goodwill and contentment, as for a new government.

clue.text: Leaders of movement against global inequality are wise men

indicators.note: leaders are those at the front, so each following word gives up its first letter

blocks.note: the initial letters of these four words

explanation.surface: The heads of a campaign against world inequality are sages.
explanation.definitionFit: The Magi are the three wise men from the East who brought gifts to the infant Jesus in the Nativity story.

clue.text: Roman emperor turned up in Florence

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit inside the following city's name
in a down clue, turned up means the letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: the run of letters inside the city's name

explanation.surface: A Roman ruler shows up in the Tuscan city of Florence.
explanation.definitionFit: Nero was the first-century emperor of Rome, notorious for persecuting Christians and allegedly fiddling while the city burned.

clue.text: German boy is extremely lonesome in Cumbria

definitions.note: names a place in Cumbria rather than defining it as a noun

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremities of the following word, its first and last letters only

blocks.note: Carl is a common German boy's name
taken as written
the first and last letters of lonesome

explanation.surface: A young German feels terribly alone while staying in England's far north-west.
explanation.walkthrough: Cumbria is a county in north-west England; its county town is Carlisle.
explanation.definitionFit: Carlisle is the main city of the county of Cumbria, near the Scottish border, so it is a place found in Cumbria.

clue.text: Strange orange beast

indicators.note: strange means odd or out of the ordinary, so the next word's letters are put into an unusual order

blocks.note: taken as written, six letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An odd-looking ginger-coloured animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The onager is a wild ass of Asia, so it is a beast in the plain sense of a wild animal.

clue.text: Princess Di and Fergie once excited stirs in Wales

indicators.note: excited means stirred up and agitated, so the letters that follow are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, twelve letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Two royal wives once caused a stir in the principality of Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: Diana married Prince Charles and Sarah Ferguson (Fergie) married his brother Andrew, making the two women related by marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: As wives of two brothers, Diana and Sarah Ferguson were each the other's in-law sibling until their divorces.

clue.text: Russia finally getting "people power" and openness

indicators.note: finally points to the end of the preceding word, keeping only its last letter

blocks.note: the last letter of Russia
people are men in the old general sense; getting signals what follows is added
power in the sense of capacity to do something

explanation.surface: Russia at last embraces people power and glasnost-style openness.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks bind 'people power' as a slogan, but people and power are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Amenability is willingness to be persuaded or receptive to ideas, which is openness of mind.

clue.text: Laid-back person with self-confidence to get higher grade

blocks.note: cat is slang for a cool, relaxed person, as in jazz talk
ego is one's sense of self-worth
to rise is to go up

explanation.surface: A relaxed, self-assured student expects a better mark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Higher grade' reads as an exam result, but grade alone is the definition, used as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To grade things is to sort them into classes by quality, which is to categorise them.

clue.text: See mothers playing games

indicators.note: playing means larking about, so the letters before it are rearranged in play

blocks.note: taken as written, ten letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Watch mums taking part in sports.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf a threesome is a match for three players, so the plural names a kind of game.

clue.text: The French girl is within the law

blocks.note: le is the French masculine word for the
gal is an informal word for a girl

explanation.surface: A young Frenchwoman is staying on the right side of the law.
explanation.definitionFit: Something legal is permitted by statute, so it sits inside what the rules allow.

clue.text: A Conservative supporting archbishop by expressing praise

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means lying underneath, so the first part comes after the archbishop

blocks.note: William Laud was Archbishop of Canterbury under Charles I
taken as written
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A right-wing politician backs a senior churchman with words of approval.
explanation.definitionFit: Laudatory describes speech or writing that praises, so it is a synonym for expressing praise.

clue.text: Pat? He's too clumsy to be a medical practitioner

indicators.note: clumsy means awkward and fumbling, so the letters of the preceding words are put together badly

blocks.note: taken as written, nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether Pat is too ham-fisted to work as a doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface jokes that a clumsy person shouldn't treat patients, yet the clumsiness is just the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An osteopath treats bodily disorders by manipulating bones and muscles, a recognised kind of medical practitioner.

clue.text: Woman's weight beginning to reduce, she declares

definitions.note: a cryptic phrase for one who declares, rather than a noun

indicators.note: the beginning of the following word means only its first letter is kept

blocks.note: Ann is a woman's name
an ounce is an imperial unit of weight
the first letter of reduce

explanation.surface: A woman about to slim down makes a public declaration of it.
explanation.walkthrough: Weight and reduce paint a dieter, but weight is just a unit and reduce supplies one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An announcer is a person who makes public statements or introduces broadcasts, so a female one is a she who declares.

clue.text: Nice, eccentric English relation

indicators.note: eccentric means off-centre or odd, so the preceding word's letters are set out of order

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
E is the standard abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A pleasant but rather odd member of the English family.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital N suggests the French city of Nice, but it is the ordinary adjective nice used as letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece is the daughter of one's brother or sister, a family relation by blood or marriage.

clue.text: Spatulas made from a phosphorus or plastic mixture

indicators.note: a mixture has its ingredients stirred together, so these letters are combined in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
P is the chemical symbol for phosphorus
taken as written

explanation.surface: Kitchen spatulas manufactured out of either a chemical element or some plastic blend.
explanation.definitionFit: Spatulas are flat tools used to spread ointments or pastes, which makes them applicators of those substances.

clue.text: Courts initially adjourned two thirds of trials

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of the following word is kept
two thirds of a six-letter word keeps four letters, so the final third is dropped

blocks.note: the first letter of adjourned
taken as written before being cut

explanation.surface: Law courts begin by postponing most of their hearings.
explanation.walkthrough: Courts looks like law courts to match adjourned and trials, but here it means courtyards.
explanation.definitionFit: Atria are open central courtyards in Roman houses or modern buildings, the plural of atrium.

clue.text: Reduce yield

blocks.note: first meaning: to cut short, as with hair
second meaning: the harvest a field produces

explanation.walkthrough: Read together the words sound like a farming instruction; they are two separate meanings of one short word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word works as a verb meaning to trim something shorter and as a noun for an agricultural harvest.

clue.text: Noise made by king cobra

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for king, from the Latin rex
an asp is a venomous snake, standing in for any cobra

explanation.surface: The sound a king cobra produces.
explanation.definitionFit: A rasp is a harsh grating sound, like that of a coarse file scraping, so it is a kind of noise.

clue.text: Think about a child

blocks.note: re means about or concerning
taken as written
a son is a male child

explanation.surface: A parent considers a youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Think about' looks like one phrase, but think is the definition and about supplies the opening letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To reason is to think logically and draw conclusions, so the verb is a synonym for thinking.

clue.text: Concern for others is a liberal cliché

blocks.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for Liberal
a truism is a statement so obvious it has become a cliché

explanation.surface: A cynic's jibe that caring about other people is just a liberal platitude.
explanation.definitionFit: Altruism is selfless regard for the welfare of other people, the opposite of selfishness.

clue.text: Dad has mostly yam and fruit

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the following word loses its last letter

blocks.note: papa is a child's word for father
joins the pieces, signalling the father possesses what follows
taken as written before being cut short

explanation.surface: Father's dinner is mainly sweet potato with some fruit on the side.
explanation.definitionFit: The papaya is a large tropical fruit with orange flesh, also called pawpaw.

clue.text: At first, spring weather's not hot; these will keep us warm

indicators.note: at first points to the opening of the following word, keeping only its initial letter
not tells us to remove the letter that stands for hot from the preceding word

blocks.note: the first letter of spring
taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Early spring is still chilly, so we wrap up in woollens.
explanation.walkthrough: H is the standard abbreviation for hot, as on taps; removing it from the weather word leaves the rest of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweaters are knitted jumpers worn for warmth, so they are garments that keep the wearer warm.
